newsitem.title: USA: PDVSA's Maraven targets Coastal refinery.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA's Maraven targets Coastal refinery.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) is moving closer to buying a stake in Coastal Corp's Corpus Cristi refinery in Texas as part of a proposed upgrading joint venture, a source at one of the companies said Friday.

Under the joint venture, PdVSA unit Maraven and Coastal would produce 90,000-100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of extra-heavy crude from the Zuata region of Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt and upgrade it into 14-16 API gravity synthetic crude for export, the sources said.
The crude would be processed at the Corpus Cristi facility, which has a capacity of 100,000 bpd and is especially suited to run sour crudes.
The deal is expected to be approved by PDVSA's board of directors in the next one to two weeks.
If approved, Maraven would seek to take a 50 percent stake in the Corpus Cristi refinery.
The venture is the sixth upgrading deal that PDVSA is aiming to implement as part of its plan to double production capacity to 6.1 million bpd in 2006.
Companies involved in other upgrading ventures include Mobil, Veba Oel, Conoco, Phillips, Arco, Texaco, Exxon and Total.
Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt contains an estimated 270 billion barrels of recoverable extra-heavy crude reserves.

PDVSA is seeking to buy stakes in several other U.S. Gulf Coast refineries, such as Mobil's 170,000 bpd Chalmette, Louisiana refinery, 200,000 bpd Phillips' Sweeny, Texas facility and the TransAmerican 60,000 bpd facility in southern Louisiana.
Under its 10-year plan, PDVSA aims to expand refining capacity to 3.5 million bpd in 2006, from 2.9 million bpd in 1997.
